_comment: Collector install. Every prompt you answer is answered a second time in the background, in a copy of your working directory, by a stock configuration - so the two can be compared. Nothing here touches your real directory, nothing is sent anywhere, and nothing leaves this machine until you run export.ps1 yourself. Set enabled to false to stop it; the hooks then do nothing at all.

copy._exclude_comment: .claude, .ssh, .aws, .gnupg and AppData are never task material and would otherwise be handed to an agent running with bypassPermissions.

_model_comment: "match" means the shadow arm runs whatever model the session is running, resolved from the transcript by the hook. Anything else pins it to that model and makes the comparison model-vs-model as much as config-vs-config - which is not what this is for. An Opus shadow run costs about 2.5x a Sonnet one, so a matched Opus session buys fewer runs out of window_budget_usd.
_keep_comment: Each run stores two copies of the project (base and work). Only the newest N runs keep them; older runs are pruned down to prompt.txt, result.json and the two patches, which is what a later comparison actually reads.
_budget_comment: Sized against what real work costs, not against a round number. Measured Opus project cells ran $2.90-$8.10, so a $2 ceiling would have cut most of them off mid-task and recorded the stub as if it were a result. $4 completes the ordinary range; anything above it is cut off by the API, comes back as subtype error_max_budget_usd, and is written to the ledger as status 'truncated' - counted, never compared. If truncated rows pile up, the prompts are bigger than the shadow budget: raise budget_usd_per_run and the purses together.
_window_comment: window_budget_usd is the ceiling for all models together (about a third of a measured 5-hour window); window_budget_by_model stops one model from eating it. The split protects sample yield, not money: each model is its own dataset, and an Opus-heavy week would otherwise leave the Sonnet arm empty. Opus runs cost roughly twice a Sonnet one, so these buy a comparable number of each.
_defer_comment: A prompt blocked by a budget is queued, not lost. The base copy is taken before the budget is checked, so a deferred run still starts from the directory as it was when the prompt arrived - the ancestor Lea diverged from. Without that the retry would begin from a tree Lea had already edited and the pair would be meaningless. Deferred runs are drained oldest-first by the next run that has budget; they expire after defer_max_age_hours and the queue is capped at defer_max_queue.
